experiment.slow_work_limits: Slow-operation logs omit fast calls. Timers overlap and counts are not all provider requests or complete causal client-time attribution.

verification.real_http: First post-checkpoint write needs a new tenant byte grant. A lost publication reply returns HTTP 200 with one debit and an unchanged exact retry receipt.
verification.negative_control: Disabling only exact-root confirmation reproduces HTTP 503 instead of 200; candidate restored immediately.
verification.adversarial: Stale observation, failed comparison before application and cancellation during confirmation grant no rights. Fresh reopening cannot rediscover spent rights; maintenance claim readback confirms one debit.

tla.bounds: One publisher, one collector, two fresh attempts and four authority revision advances; historical positive observations, missing replies, one-time confirmation and abort. Component check, not complete protocol composition or Rust refinement.

removed: Replaced unconditional propagation of tenant publication uncertainty with one bounded exact-root readback.
Updated blanket lost-reply wording; stale observations retain the existing refusal tests.
Reused the publication model and TCP fixture instead of adding parallel protocols or harnesses.
Restored the temporary negative-control mutation and removed generated model state directories.
limitations: The previous B2 preparation error did not record its precise cause; the fault regression proves this failure class, not that every earlier delay had this cause.
Confirmation requires the exact staged tenant-directory root. Superseding ledger changes, stale absence, failed reads and cancellation remain uncertain; namespace grants are unchanged.
Short closed-loop matrix with randomized placement and variable provider conditions; no general performance, sustained-load, p99 or availability SLO claim.
Funding readback counts are observed confirmations, not provider billing or a complete breakdown of delays.
Existing single-trust-domain 1.0 support scope is unchanged.
